ranking.reason: When C2[j-1] (or C1[j-1]) takes over as C1[j], its color isn't checked against the pushed-down C1[j]; stale V1[j] moved to C2[j] could share the new C1[j]'s color, breaking the two-distinct-color invariant.
elif only checks incoming color against C1[j]; if V2[j-1] has same color as new C1[j] after a swap in the first branch it can be accepted incorrectly, and tie handling with old C2[j] is lost.
On repeated color for j=0, discarding to -INF instead of carrying a valid alternative may lose reachable states.
V2[j]+vi assumes V2[j] has a different color and is a valid predecessor; no guard that V2[j] was set.
Blindly adding vi when C1[j] != ci trusts the invariant that previous state had distinct alternate color; can compound earlier invariant breakage.
